To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass transportation in the galactic disk, as a result of self-consistent N-body interactions, influences the character of orbits in a way that is consistent with our expectations.

the percentage of chaotic motion is significantly increased as the nucleus develops and becomes denser and more massive, whereas the percentage of orbits of the various regular families is reduced accordingly, and the percentage of chaotic stars is increased at the expense of the regular ones.

(i) mass transport in the disk of the galaxy model under consideration does not affect the orbital structure of stars moving in meridional plane of the model, (ii) the amount of chaos is substantially increased when the nucleus of the galaxy is becoming more massive and (iii) there are orbits which are regular and chaotic at different times of the galactic evolution, while there are orbits that keep their nature unchanged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamical evolution of a galaxy and the influence of mass transportation in the disk on the character of the stellar orbits.
the dynamical effects of the formation of a dense nucleus in the core of a disk galaxy, and how the mass transport from the disk to this nucleus influences the character of orbits of the stars.
the dynamical evolution of disk galaxy models with a time-dependent mass transport and with the influence of this transport on the character of orbits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of chaos is not only a result of the self-gravitational forces acting in an actual disk galaxy but it is also due to the presence of a dense and massive galactic nucleus.
the chaotic orbits are more abundant in the outer regions of the disk galaxy model.

the mass transport from disk to nucleus, which is a common phenomenon in galactic evolution, is not a factor that can be neglected, as it can substantially influence the character of orbits of the stellar component of a galaxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chaoticity of the motion is increased as the nucleus of the galaxy becomes more massive.
the mass transportation from the disk to its nucleus, which leads to the formation of a massive nucleus, has a strong impact on the orbital dynamics of the stars in the galactic disk.
the chaotic orbits are not only created during the galactic formation but they also increase during the galactic dynamical evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chaotic nature of orbits in disk galaxies can be influenced by the mass transport from the disk to a massive galactic nucleus.

the mass transportation from the disk to a galactic nucleus, as it happens in actual galactic simulations, is not expected to have a significant effect on the character of the orbits of the stars, at least for the cases studied here.
the chaotic orbits are not confined to the central region of the galaxy, but they extend up to the disk plane.
